EPISODE_NARRATIVE: As an upper level low moved through the region, severe thunderstorms developed along a weak cold front that moved through North Dakota. Scattered showers and non-severe thunderstorms were ongoing during the morning before increasing in strength throughout the afternoon. A cluster of severe thunderstorms moved through parts of north central North Dakota, including the Turtle Mountains area, before additional storms developed to the south in the James River Valley area. |The most significant damage occurred approximately 4 miles northeast of Belcourt. Multiple buildings were damaged at a collection of properties in this area. A garage on the southwest side of the damage area lost a section of its roof that video and drone footage show was blown northeast across the property. The other main building with damage is a residential home at the center property that lost a significant portion of its roof ripped off. On the north and east side of this property, there were multiple hardwood trees damaged, some snapped about halfway down, but all generally extending to the northeast. A utility truck was parked at the center property and was facing south when the storm came through. A two by four plank of wood went through the windshield and both occupants of the truck had minor injuries. At the eastern property in this group, a shed collapsed and was blown into the edge of a wooded area to the northeast. Drone footage shows numerous trees damaged in this wooded area, extending a few hundred feet northeast of the buildings on the property. Winds were estimated at 95 mph. To the northeast, there was another property with approximately 15 to 20 oak trees that were damaged. |The other main area of damage occurred in Stutsman County, one mile west of Spiritwood. A 200 foot by 60 foot barn was blown over and dismantled. Based on photo and satellite imagery, barn was oriented west-east with 3 doors facing south. The storm was moving from south to north, which would be a favorable direction to funnel wind into the broad side of the barn with multiple doors, helping the barn collapse and push pieces into the tree row directly to the north. This is consistent with wind speeds of around 85 mph.|The highest measured wind gust was 62 mph near Zeeland in Mcintosh County and near Pettibone in Kidder County. The largest hail reported was golf ball sized, west of Belcourt in Rolette County.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Hail up to the size of quarters that lasted about 10 minutes.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: An upper level low and surface cold front combined with a very unstable airmass resulted in severe thunderstorms across western and central North Dakota. Supercell thunderstorms initially produced very large hail before transitioning to a linear storm mode, which led to widespread significant thunderstorm wind gusts. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, occurring southwest of Medora in Billings County. Measured wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common as storms moved across western and central North Dakota. The area with the most significant wind damage occurred across Stark, Morton, Mercer, and McLean Counties. In a swath from Dickinson, to Hebron, to Beulah, to Douglas Bay, to west of Garrison, damage from thunderstorm wind gusts led to winds estimated from 80 to 100 mph. The strongest measured wind gust came from a personal weather station just east of Beulah that reported a gust of 103 mph. Damage included campers turned over, large trees downed, roof damage, power outages, garages destroyed, vehicle damage, siding damage, and dented grain bins.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough and low-level jet combined with a very moist and unstable air mass that led to severe thunderstorm development along the triple point of a surface low in west central North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon in southwest North Dakota, with additional storms in the far northwest. Storms gradually moved to the north-northeast through the evening in a primarily cluster storm mode. The area of most significant damage was in Ward and McHenry Counties. In the town of Sawyer in Ward County, the Emergency Manager reported damage from powerful thunderstorm wind gusts that resulted in power outages, trees on roads, and a large tree that fell onto a house and made a hole in the roof. Northeast of Deering in McHenry County, there was significant damage to a homestead due to thunderstorm wind gusts. A barn on the property had roof panels ripped off and some collapse of the wood frame structure for the roof. Damage in both of these locations were consistent with wind speeds around 90 mph. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, a few miles west of Fortuna in Divide County. One tornado occurred with these storms, and was reported approximately 3 miles east of Noonan in Divide County. It was a very brief tornado and caused no known damage, so has been rated EF-Unknown by NWS policy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough and low-level jet combined with a very moist and unstable air mass that led to severe thunderstorm development along the triple point of a surface low in west central North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon in southwest North Dakota, with additional storms in the far northwest. Storms gradually moved to the north-northeast through the evening in a primarily cluster storm mode. The area of most significant damage was in Ward and McHenry Counties. In the town of Sawyer in Ward County, the Emergency Manager reported damage from powerful thunderstorm wind gusts that resulted in power outages, trees on roads, and a large tree that fell onto a house and made a hole in the roof. Northeast of Deering in McHenry County, there was significant damage to a homestead due to thunderstorm wind gusts. A barn on the property had roof panels ripped off and some collapse of the wood frame structure for the roof. Damage in both of these locations were consistent with wind speeds around 90 mph. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, a few miles west of Fortuna in Divide County. One tornado occurred with these storms, and was reported approximately 3 miles east of Noonan in Divide County. It was a very brief tornado and caused no known damage, so has been rated EF-Unknown by NWS policy.

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A surface trough and low-level jet combined with a very moist and unstable air mass that led to severe thunderstorm development along the triple point of a surface low in west central North Dakota. Thunderstorms developed during the afternoon in southwest North Dakota, with additional storms in the far northwest. Storms gradually moved to the north-northeast through the evening in a primarily cluster storm mode. The area of most significant damage was in Ward and McHenry Counties. In the town of Sawyer in Ward County, the Emergency Manager reported damage from powerful thunderstorm wind gusts that resulted in power outages, trees on roads, and a large tree that fell onto a house and made a hole in the roof. Northeast of Deering in McHenry County, there was significant damage to a homestead due to thunderstorm wind gusts. A barn on the property had roof panels ripped off and some collapse of the wood frame structure for the roof. Damage in both of these locations were consistent with wind speeds around 90 mph. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, a few miles west of Fortuna in Divide County. One tornado occurred with these storms, and was reported approximately 3 miles east of Noonan in Divide County. It was a very brief tornado and caused no known damage, so has been rated EF-Unknown by NWS policy.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Storm chaser reported brief tornado at this approximate location. No known damage to evaluate and no other information available. By National Weather Service policy the tornado is rated EF-U (Unknown).

EPISODE_NARRATIVE: A warm front lifted across North Dakota while strong southerly surface flow increased temperatures and dew points over the region. As a surface trough tracked to the east, storms developed in eastern Montana and moved into western North Dakota during the evening. Storms quickly formed a line as they continued moving east-northeast, with powerful wind gusts the primary hazard across western and portions of central North Dakota. A tornado occurred approximately 7 miles north-northeast of Belfield in Billings County. The track was less than one mile long and wind speeds were estimated up to 90 mph, leading to an EF-1 rating. Damaging wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common across the area as storms moved through. The most significant damage occurred in a neighborhood west of Williston. The Emergency Manager reported debris in a southwest to northeast orientation, consistent with straight line winds. Notable damage includes two homes with roofs uplifted and partially blown off. Other damage includes sheds, enclosed trailers, and campers damaged or destroyed. Some tree damage was also noted. Damage is consistent with wind speeds around 95 mph.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: Personal weather station reported wind gusts up to 59 mph.

An upper level low and surface cold front combined with a very unstable airmass resulted in severe thunderstorms across western and central North Dakota. Supercell thunderstorms initially produced very large hail before transitioning to a linear storm mode, which led to widespread significant thunderstorm wind gusts. The largest reported hail was 3 inches in diameter, occurring southwest of Medora in Billings County. Measured wind gusts of 60 to 80 mph were common as storms moved across western and central North Dakota. The area with the most significant wind damage occurred across Stark, Morton, Mercer, and McLean Counties. In a swath from Dickinson, to Hebron, to Beulah, to Douglas Bay, to west of Garrison, damage from thunderstorm wind gusts led to winds estimated from 80 to 100 mph. The strongest measured wind gust came from a personal weather station just east of Beulah that reported a gust of 103 mph. Damage included campers turned over, large trees downed, roof damage, power outages, garages destroyed, vehicle damage, siding damage, and dented grain bins.
EVENT_NARRATIVE: A brief, dusty tornado touched down southeast of Bowbells. The tornado formed and soon after knocked over a grain bin and sheared off the top half of pine trees. The tornado then tracked to the northeast for a couple of miles before dissipating before reaching the river. This tornado continued into Ward County. Based on the damage done this tornado was rated EF-1, and from that wind speeds were estimated to be around 95 mph.
